Great game! It's like going back in time 20 years, but without the potato graphics. It's actually a pretty lengthy campaign too, and the soundtrack that kicks in from time to time is excellent and fits the feel of the game well.
It took me a little while to unlearn 20 years worth of RMB = ADS, and it does have some glitches (like items falling through floors, some weird "airhockey table" like effect where everything slides around, and random loss of some SFX). Don't let that put you off though, it's fairly rare and easily fixed in a matter of seconds simply by dropping a save and restarting the game. The only real downside is when you finish it, you remember HL3 is still only a pipe dream.

TL;DR - Fans of the original HL and "veteran" gamers looking for a retro FPS fix will love this.

As an almost complete newcomer to the Half-Life franchise, I greatly enjoyed my time with Black Mesa. An old school shooter through and through, Black Mesa feels refreshingly simple in it's approach to combat, narrative and overall gameplay. While the textures and effects aren't be on par with most modern games nowadays, the artstyle, atmosphere and setpieces are impressive in of themselves and the devs really used the Source Engine to it's full potential. I do have some gripes though, mainly with the marines and Xen. While the combat is fun, and you're given a varied arsenal of weapons, I found the marine encounters to be unfairly tough and annoying at times. Because of their hitscan attacks and ability to fire at you the moment you get out from cover, some of the later levels where you're up against 8 or more of them devolved into trial and error rather than an organic and balanced fight. Now onto Xen, which for the most part was graphically stunning and a joy to explore, but later chapters (especially "Interloper") seemed to slog on a bit too long with not much to see or do besides some tedious platforming and puzzles. Overall though, highly recomended.

Black Mesa, as advertised. An excellently done and faithful recreation and revamp of the original Half-Life, this game brings a previously ancient and rusting experience into the modern day, with all the love and attention it deserves.

Visuals: 10/10
Excellently done graphical effects, UI and menus are high quality, no bugs, no glitches, simple to use and understand.
Game looks like a treat, and generally runs like one too, although this is a rather demanding game.

Audio: 10/10
Audio is a treat as well, excellent ambience, variety of configurations to support surround sound systems, well balanced, and very well chosen sounds mean that it never gets old either.

Gameplay: 9/10
No significant gameplay issues. Mostly straight forward combat (with varying difficulty, encounters, a vast number of enemy types, and some stealth and surprise opportunities), simple puzzle solving, A few boss fights, and linear game progression. Confusing level layouts occasionally leave something to be desired. Did experience crashes multiple times involving the controllers and vortigaunts when they're being controlled. Keeps things fresh as the game progresses, you're never dealing with the same enemy encounters more than you can handle.

---/// Overall: 9.7/10 ///---

A love letter to the community and a labor of love. Despite all the hurdles and struggles during development, Crowbar Collective managed to treat Half-Life community with a great re-imagining of iconic first Half-Life game.

Black Mesa offers slightly different take on Half-Life, while keeping core gameplay and game design aspects ( in some places expanding them ) close to a vanilla game. It's really hard for me to lambaste this game for anything, without sounding too nitpicky, but I'm sure there's some aspects of it some die hard fans had voiced their opinions about.

Black Mesa had a long run, it transitioned from being a top-notch free mod into Valve quality Source Engine game, and despite all odds and thanks to dedicated development team it still keeps evolving to this day. Crowbar Collective deserves all the support they could get for taking such a monstrous task on their shoulders and I sincerely hope this is not the last game/remake from them. I still love to reminiscing on old Black Mesa : Source development videos just to see how much love and effort was put into this project, even at the free mod stage.

I wish Crowbar Collective best of luck in finishing remaining Xen chapters and in their future endeavours.

Xen is still absolute shit. It's MUCH better than the original - it feels like an actual living world and very good looking visually. Exploring the research sites was pretty great.

However it gets very tedious after an hour or so. Navigating is hard since you always get stuck on something. Jump boost works differently on every jump. Had to turn on noclip numerous times because I got stuck in the terrain. Every puzzle is repeated a billion times. The last sections are padded out for no reason. The elevator section before the last boss has no reason to exist.
Shit, if you love the original Half Life 1 or new to the series and want to experience the original Half Life 1 in a more high quality game, I recommend this dearly!

The best game in history. An incredible retelling of the original with flawless storytelling that stays true to the source material, stunning graphics, and redesigned combat that feels more meaningful to the story. It also expands on parts of the Half-Life lore that the original game never explored in such depth.

If you're wondering whether you should buy it, don't hesitate. I've beaten the original Half-Life six times, and not once did I enjoy it as much as I enjoyed the 11 hours this masterpiece gave me. Now it's my turn to 100% the game—your turn is to experience it for yourself.

Opportunities like this don't come around often, so don't miss it.

Thank you, Crowbar Collective, for creating this masterpiece.

This isn't just a game, it's a labor of love that became a work of art. If you are a fan of classic shooters, or if you want to go back to the roots to see how we got to where we are today...you've come to the right place!

This amazing fan/community REMAKE of the entire original game is one of the most impressive undertakings I've ever seen. When I hear "remake" or "remaster" or something along those lines in the gaming industry, I think of AAA studios throwing a minimum effort at a cash cow to make a few bucks. Not this.

Each environment, interaction, scripted event...EVERYTHING has been painstakingly re-created and updated. If you've played the original game, you'll quickly see that this isn't a fresh coat of paint, it's like trading in your Ford Model A and getting back a Tesla...the concepts and the bones are all there, but it's entirely modernized and breathes incredible new life into the game! If you're on the fence, take my word and buy it. You won't be disappointed!

A remake of Half-Life, with Half-Life 2 models and engine. It still follows the original game's story and locations, with some changes. The enemies here are unusually dangerous (even on Easy) and it's kinda hard to navigate in dark places. The thing I don't like about this game is that sometimes it's confusing to know which way to go, and since this game is technically fanmade and a remake, not many good walkthroughs appear. The developers expanded the final levels, the alien world Xen greatly, it feels like a game of its own. If you want a good experience playing an updated Half-Life, this game is a must buy.

You should just play the original instead. It's cheaper, runs better, and is more stable, and probably will look about the same since even with a decent graphics card it needs to drop it to "Potato" quality (the lowest settings) to get over 30 FPS. Some of the achievements will bug the game unless you do very specific sequence of events leading up to them.

Masterful recreation of the original Half-Life with much better graphics. Black Mesa started as a modification but became an independent game with the blessing of Valve. Even though the game is made by fans of Half-Life, it is very well done. It honestly feels as if Valve themselves had made it. Black Mesa perfectly captures the magic and feel of the original game. While some minor details are different from the original, it doesn't deviate from it too much. Also, the soundtrack is awesome.
The only negative thing I have to say about this game is that it's not finished yet. It's still in an early access state and the final "Xen" chapters are missing because they're not ready yet and their release have been delayed way too many times. Once the Xen levels are ready however (hopefully this year), they will be given as a free update to all players and then the game will move out of early access. If you want to play the Xen levels, just play the original Half-Life until the Xen update is released.

9/10 Would smack headcrabs with a crowbar again.

I was very much enjoying Black Mesa, however the Xen chapters rather spoilt things, to a degree that this game really does not deserve a 95% positive rating. I found the last three hours of the game unfun, and felt myself grimly slogging through just to see the end.

Up to the Xen chapter, all is good, however the Xen third of the game wildly overstays it's welcome and is in desperate need of editing down. There are some mildly dull puzzle sections and somewhat janky action sections, both of which go on 2-3 *times* longer than they need to (imagine working out and correctly solving a puzzle, then doing very slight variations on the same umpteen times). It reminds me of the old joke of two men complaining about a restaurant; "the food was terrible, and the portions!"
